description: 57-year-old female former smoker incidentally found to have a hypermetabolic left upper lobe lesion confirmed as poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma; no cough or idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis reported.
History: Patient A is a 57 year old female former smoker who presented to the office complaining of pain from a MVA. She reports that she was a front seat passenger in a vehicle that was stopped when it was was struck from behind by another vehicle. She reports that her knee struck the dashboard but reports no loss of consciousness, no blood loss and that no ambulance was summoned. She reports that she went on her own to a local hospital later that week. She reports that she was examined, radiographs were performed, and medication was prescribed prior to her discharge. The patient reports that she then consulted her PCP who examined her and referred her for physical therapy. She received PT for two weeks. Care included: exercise, stretching, and the use of a heat pad on her neck. The patient reports that later she went to another physical therapy facility where care included exercises and stretches. She reports last receiving care at this facility until four months prior to the initial visit to the office. She reports consulting with an orthopedic surgeon who examined her and sent her to get an MRI of her spine. Based on the images, the surgeon did not recommend surgery at that time. She also consulted a pain management specialist who provided pain medication. Three months after the initial visit she patient was experiencing left arm pain that radiated to the left axilla and chest. She was sent for a shoulder x-ray to assess her condition. An incidental finding on the x-ray prompted her to get a CT of the chest a month later which revealed a 3.2 x 1.5 cm left upper lobe mass. There was also a right lung nodule measuring approximately 1 cm in size. She was referred to the local cancer institute for further evaluation. She underwent PET-CT imaging a month after the initial CT and had an endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) with biopsy in the same month. The PET scan revealed a left lung mass with a SUV of 21.4. The other nodule was not hypermetabolic. There was uptake in the right lobe of the thyroid as well as in a lymph node inferior to the thyroid and was referred to the thyroid clinic for further evaluation of these findings. The EBUS with biopsy was negative for malignancy, therefore was sent for CT guided biopsy. The pathology report for this biopsy returned invasive, poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the left upper lung. She then underwent an MRI of her brain to rule out metastases and a further workup was done to determine whether the patient was a surgical candidate. It was determined that the cancer was only local and that the patient was a surgical candidate. Patient B is a 73 year old female who was involved in a MVA occurring around the same time as patient A. At that time, she was employed as a cleaner for a business. She worked for this business for 5 years but lost time at work as a result of the accident. The patient reports that she was the restrained driver of a vehicle making a left turn at a light when she was struck by another vehicle on the passenger side. She reports brief LOC but regained consciousness while still in the car. No blood loss was reported nor was an ambulance called. She went to a local hospital where radiographs were obtained and pain medication and muscle relaxants were prescribed. She was advised to contact her PCP with her other concerns: difficulty standing, walking, riding, bending, twisting, heavy/repetitive lifting, and sleeping. At the time of the accident, the patient reported left chest and rib pain feeling shortness of breath but that the SOB resolved shortly after the accident. However, several months later, the patient still complained of left chest and rib pain since the accident. The patient was sent for CT of the chest 5 months later for rib pain and to rule out rib fracture. It was noted that she had a spiculated semi-solid opacity present posteriorly at the right apex measuring approximately 2.0 cm in its greatest diameter. It was recommended that she follow up with a PET-CT to rule out malignancy. The patient underwent PET-CT 2 months after the CT which confirmed a spiculated focus at the right lung apex. However, the lesion did not show significant metabolic activity (SUV max 1.4) and it was determined that it was most likely chronic scarring. The patient was advised to undergo a follow up CT in one year to document stability of the lesion.

description: 71-year-old male with a significant history of smoking; idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis not mentioned.
History: The patient reports being diagnosed with lung cancer several years ago. Prior to being diagnosed with cancer he has had COPD for decades. The cancer diagnosed is in the left lung from the hilar region to the apex of the left upper lobe. He received PET CT evaluation and subsequent lung resection. He was placed on Chemotherapy and did well with the treatment.Unfortunately cancer returned into his left lung. He indicates that he was going to try immunotherapy which was a procedure performed every 2 weeks for the rest of his life. Unfortunately, he had devastating effects from the immunotherapy making his ability to breath worse and called hospice in January 2021. He reports that they brought him oxygen and medications some of which were morphine, sleeping pills and methadone. However, the medications were just too much for the patient to handle on a day to day basis and as such he cut back on the medications. He reports that the chemotherapy that he received earlier on worked in a very adverse manner to the rest of his body with numbness and tingling in his hands and feet as well as a difficulty in actually thinking. He had a discussion with the doctor at hospice and was told that he had 2 months to live. However that has been over a year now. He had been going to physical therapy for strengthening and conditioning. He received the double vax of the MRNA vaccine in March of 2021. He has been getting stronger up until September of this year when he took the booster. He then had difficulty breathing after such. This continued until December of 2021 when he contracted Covid. He reports not recovering from the vaccine effects prior to Covid and had not recovered from the effects of Covid either at this point. He is very tired and is on 3 liters of oxygen/minute 24/7 and uses a portable oxygen generator that he purchased himself for $2700.Up until recently he indicated that the cancer hospital had no further suggestions or treatment when he was with hospice. However, he has been followed closely with imaging and there is indication that the tumor sizes have gotten larger between October 2021 and January 2022. He is now faced with a conundrum. He is being asked to leave the care of hospice so that he can receive chemotherapy. If he does so, he also loses monetary coverage for his oxygen and medicines. He will likely do so however as another round of chemotherapy is being suggested. His goal is to ride his bicycle in the fund raiser for the cancer hospital in the summer likely with his oxygen supply. He is eating healthy and having good bowel movements. He utilizes an albuterol breathing exercise and does spirometry exercises. He eats vitamins, organic food and takes protein powder. The patient has had a long history of lower back symptoms. He has had periodic lower back and right lower extremity pain.The lower back and right lower extremity pain began approximately 5-6 years ago. He does not feel that this symptom is related to a vehicular accident though he has been in such in the past.PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:The patient reports that 15-16 years ago while at work, he was struck in the upper back region. He received chiropractic care and made a full recovery.The patient reports that over 40 years ago, the vehicle he was in was struck from behind by another vehicle. He reports that he had back and neck pain as a result.Approximately 17 years ago he tripped over his brotherâ€™s dog and crashed onto the floor. He reports that he had back pain as a result. He reports that he had radiographs taken of his knees and lower back when he was 50 years old and such demonstrated arthritis in each areas. He reports that he fractured his left wrist when he was 13 years old.He denies cardiovascular problems, other neurological problems, endocrine issues, renal problems, gastroenterological problems, hematological problems, or psychological issues. He reports having eczema. He also reports having osteoarthritis. Surgical: Left ear cyst removal Smoking: 50 pack year smoker. Quit 2017. Occupational: Worked as a machinist, exposure to asbestos Family: One brother and one sister each with brain cancer.

description: 49-year-old male smoker with neurological and respiratory symptoms; idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis not mentioned.
History: CHIEF COMPLAINT: A 49-year-old male with a two-week history of right upper extremity weakness, loss of fine motor skills, and troubles with gait,presenting with mass in the lung and brain by CT exam and MRI, status postbronchoscopy with pathology pending. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 49-year-old male who is anative of Saint Croix. Approximately two weeks ago, he began noticing the first of several difficulties. He had problems with fine motor skills and difficulty inholding his pen. His problems were on his right side. He isright-handed. He noticed also some gait abnormalities and trouble with placement of his right foot. He also began to develop headaches soonafter, which woke him up at night from sleep. He was initially givenPercocet and had no relief from this medication. He next tried ibuprofen andNaprosyn with some relief. He denied any vision changes, hearing trouble,speech problems, or eating difficulty at any point. Last Friday, he drove to a local clinic for evaluation. His primary presenting complaint was loss of fine motor skills in his right extremities and difficulty walking. Initial CT of the head without contrast was ordered. The findingsrevealed masses within the brain with brain edema in the left hemispheresuperior to the left lateral ventricle with midline shift. He was airlifted to a medical treatment facility for further evaluation. REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: The patient notes no fevers, however, he has had chills and nightsweats over the last two weeks. He also notes 17-pound weight loss for thelast four months. Furthermore, he also has noted word-finding difficulty in the last two weeks with some memory loss. He also has gait difficulties andsome fine motor skill difficulties on the right side. He denies any left-sided difficulties and only motor deficits on the right side. No sensory deficits. SOCIAL HISTORY: He smoked cigarettes for approximately 20 years, one packper day for a 20-pack year history. He quit smoking5 months ago.
